items.title: Flex-RSI: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement of Frontier Agents
items.summary_1line: Frontier language models are increasingly deployed as agents, and how well an agent performs depends not only on its model but also on its harness: the prompts, tools, memory, and control loop through which the model...
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, eval.
items.editor_note: RSI를 하네스 중심으로 재정립하고, 프런티어 에이전트가 하네스를 개선하는 능력을 측정하는 벤치마크를 추가했다.

items.title: Trustworthy Recursive Self-Improvement with Statistical Guarantees
items.summary_1line: Recursive self-improvement offers a promising path toward AI agents that improve through experience by refining their own harnesses without retraining their underlying large language models (LLMs). Making this self-im...
items.editor_note: 통계적 보증을 도입해 하네스 자기 수정이 증거가 있을 때만 채택되도록 했다.

items.title: SciMARS: Multi-Agent Recursive Self-Improvement for Closed-Loop Scientific Discovery
items.summary_1line: We propose SciMARS, a framework for recursive task-local adaptation of multi-agent harnesses in closed-loop scientific discovery. Multi-agent systems coordinate analysis, experimental design, and verification as scien...

items.editor_note: 하네스 RSI를 단일 에이전트에서 멀티 에이전트 과학 발견 루프로 확장했다.

items.title: BaseRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement of a Base Vision-Language Model via Training-Free Harness Internalization
items.summary_1line: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) is moving from the harness of prompts and tools around a base model toward the model itself. However, existing RSI still faces key challenges, including harness-bound gains that stay o...
items.editor_note: 학습 없이 하네스에서 얻은 성능 향상을 기반 비전-언어 모델로 옮긴다.

items.title: Piccolo: Co-Evolving Decision Models and Data through Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary_1line: We present Piccolo, a family of multimodal decision models (0.8B to 27B) that coevolves model capabilities and training data via Agentic Data Engineering and recursive self-improvement (RSI). The models predict probab...
items.editor_note: 모델 가중치와 학습 데이터를 함께 진화시키며, 0.8B에서 27B까지 아우르는 모델 패밀리를 제시한다.

items.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
items.summary_1line: Proposes TT-RSI, a label-free test-time framework that re-solves questions using earlier solutions as references and distills refinements into model weights, reporting a +13.89% average accuracy gain over the base model.
items.editor_note: 레이블 없이 테스트 시점에 RSI를 적용하고, 개선 결과를 가중치로 증류해 평균 +13.89% 향상을 보고했다.

items.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
items.summary_1line: Introduces RecurSciBench, a benchmark that auto-builds executable scientific modeling and data analysis tasks across four domains to test whether AI agents improve through recursive self-improvement and transfer that gain to new tasks.
items.editor_note: 네 개 도메인에서 자기 개선이 새로운 과제로 전이되는지 검증하도록 설계한 두 번째 과학 벤치마크다.

items.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
items.summary_1line: RoboEvo² is a robot learning framework in which a coding agent and a vision-language-action policy iteratively improve each other, reporting higher success on LIBERO-PRO and RoboTwin C2R without added human demonstrations.
items.editor_note: 최초의 임바디드 루프로, 코딩 에이전트와 VLA 정책이 새로운 사람 시연 없이 서로를 개선한다.

editorial.tldr: Early November's recursive self-improvement (RSI) papers had agents rewrite their own harness (prompts, tools, memory, control loop) with the base model frozen, and added a benchmark, a statistical acceptance test, and a multi-agent science version. From Nov 18 the loop moved into the weights: BaseRSI, Piccolo, and test-time TT-RSI each fold self-generated gains back into the model.
editorial.whats_new: RSI now has a second science benchmark and its first robotics loop: RecurSciBench (Nov 24) tests whether agents' self-improvement transfers to new tasks, and RoboEvo² (Nov 25) has a coding agent and a VLA policy improve each other.
editorial.why_it_matters: Self-improving loops now edit harnesses, weights, and robot policies, so the harness and every self-edit become versioned artifacts that need held-out evals, transfer checks, and rollback.
editorial.take_for_builders: If your agent edits its own prompts, tools, memory, or weights, version every self-edit and gate it on a held-out eval of unseen tasks, with a rollback path, before it reaches production.

beats.headline: Harness RSI gets a benchmark and a statistical safety check
beats.summary: Flex-RSI scores how well frontier agents improve their own harness; a second paper accepts a self-edit only with statistical evidence that it helps.

beats.headline: SciMARS applies recursive harness adaptation to multi-agent scientific discovery
beats.summary: Analysis, experiment design, and verification agents adapt their shared harness task by task in a closed loop.

beats.headline: RSI moves from the harness back into the model
beats.summary: BaseRSI internalizes harness gains without training, Piccolo co-evolves a 0.8B-27B model family with its data, and TT-RSI distills test-time refinements into weights.

beats.headline: Transfer benchmarks and an embodied loop
beats.summary: RecurSciBench checks whether self-improvement carries to new science tasks; RoboEvo² co-evolves a robot harness and policy.

open_questions: Does Flex-RSI or RecurSciBench publish per-model scores that show which frontier agents actually gain from self-improvement?
Do statistical acceptance tests for self-edits hold when the eval distribution shifts after deployment?
Does BaseRSI's training-free internalization keep its gains on tasks outside the harness it learned from?
Does TT-RSI's label-free +13.89% gain survive on benchmarks where earlier solutions are often wrong?
Do RoboEvo²'s simulation gains on LIBERO-PRO and RoboTwin carry over to real robots?
